summary: Tenant-claim namespace stripping causes service tokens to be treated as cross-tenant and return 403 in private prod
description:
Issue summary:
FinSight reports that internal service-to-service API calls using service account JWTs are intermittently receiving 403 responses from Redwood's private deployment. The tokens are valid and accepted by the IdP, but when routed through the customer's private ingress + idp-proxy, Redwood's authz layer is evaluating them as belonging to a different tenant.

Impact:
- Production job-workers (data enrichment pipeline) failing to call Redwood inference endpoints for multiple customers of FinSight; ~30% of calls hit 403s over the last 8 hours.
- Customer-facing processing delays and retries causing downstream SLA breaches.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer VPC) in us-east-1
- Ingress: customer-managed ALB -> edge-proxy (Redwood idp-proxy) -> private control plane
- Customer service tokens are short-lived JWTs minted by the customer's IdP (Okta) and include tenant-scoped claim "tid" in the namespaced claim key: "https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid"

Observed behaviour:
- Tokens accepted by the introspection endpoint; token introspection shows "tid" present. However, once request reaches authz policy evaluation, tenant resolution falls back to default_tenant and policy denies access.

Hypothesis:
- The private ingress or our claim-normalization middleware is stripping or rewriting namespaced claim keys (removing the URL prefix) resulting in a mismatch with tenant routing (we expect full namespaced claim name). If the claim key is altered (e.g., becomes "tid" instead of "https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid"), tenant lookup fails and request is treated as cross-tenant.

Why this is different from previous tickets:
- Many prior SSO issues were related to whitespace, case sensitivity, or trailing-dot hostnames. This appears to be an interpolation/sanitizer that removes characters from claim keys (slash or colon) when certain ingress header transformations are present on the customer's ALB.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer mints short-lived service account JWT with namespaced claim key 'https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid' and value 'tenant-1234'.
2) Send request to Redwood private inference endpoint via customer's ALB with header Authorization: Bearer <token>.
3) Observe 403 from authz; call token introspection endpoint to confirm token validity (returns active:true and shows claim key).
4) Re-run with the same token but bypassing the ALB (direct route to edge-proxy) — request succeeds.
5) Capture ingress request headers at edge-proxy when routed via ALB vs bypassed.
logs:
edge-proxy (via ALB) log snippet:
[2026-03-14T02:14:03Z] request_id=0a1b authz:received_claims={"tid":"tenant-1234", "sub":"svc-account-9"} tenant_resolution=default_tenant decision=DENY reason='tenant claim missing namespaced_key'

edge-proxy (direct) log snippet:
[2026-03-14T02:12:19Z] request_id=ff4c authz:received_claims={"https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid":"tenant-1234", "sub":"svc-account-9"} tenant_resolution=tenant-1234 decision=ALLOW

ALB header transformation trace (customer-provided): 'X-Forwarded-User-Claims' truncated slashes and replaced ':' with '_' in header serialization.

investigation_notes:
- 2026-03-13 20:05: Local repro: created middleware that rewrites 'https://finsight.example.com/claims/tid' to 'tid' and tenant resolution failed.
- 2026-03-13 21:00: Confirmed that token introspection still returns original claim keys (IdP shows namespaced key) — transformation happens at ingress header serialization step on the ALB.
- 2026-03-13 22:15: Authz's claim-normalizer currently performs exact-key lookup for tenant claims and falls back to a blacklist-safe default tenant if not found. There's no canonicalization path for rewritten claim keys.
- 2026-03-14 00:40: Tested tolerant lookup that attempts both namespaced and suffix-key match (i.e., check full key then strip URL prefix and check again) — tenant resolution succeeds in repro.
- 2026-03-14 02:00: Security review: tolerant lookup could create ambiguity if two tenants choose colliding short claim names. Decided to scope change to 'private' deployments where customer-provided claim namespace is configured in tenant mapping.
resolution:
Workaround applied and patch submitted:
- Short-term workaround: Instructed FinSight to disable ALB JSON key sanitization (passthrough namespaced claim keys). This immediately restored traffic (customer confirmed success after 20 minutes).
- Medium-term fix: Auth team implemented tolerant tenant-lookup in private deployments that consults tenant mapping for both full namespaced claim keys and the suffix-only key. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth/pull/319 (under review).
- Rollout plan: patch gated behind feature flag 'private.tolerant_claim_lookup' and will be deployed to staging for canary in prod next 24 hours. Monitoring: added metric 'auth.tolerant_lookup_matches' and alert if mismatch rate > 0.5% after rollout.
follow_up_actions: 1) Auth Eng to complete security review and merge PR 319 (ETA 2026-03-15)
2) Deploy feature-flagged change to staging and run regression tests against known claim mangling patterns (owner: Priya Nair)
3) Update Private Deploy runbook to document ALB header serialization caveat and customer guidance (owner: Support)
4) Outreach to other private customers to check for similar ALB/edge configurations (CS team to create a short checklist)
5) Close ticket after 48h stable canary and customer confirmation
